record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Classify semigroups from the basic classes of semigroups up to inclusive equivalence, meaning that they satisfy the same identical inclusions or, equivalently, generate the same inclusive variety.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.4. (G. Mashevitzky) Classify semigroups from the basic classes of semigroups up to
inclusive equivalence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S$ be a semigroup. An identical inclusion on $S$ is a formal expression of the form
$$ w(x_1,\dots,x_n) \in \{w_1(x_1,\dots,x_n),\, w_2(x_1,\dots,x_n),\,\dots\}, $$
where $w$ and the $w_i$ are words in the free semigroup on the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$. The semigroup $S$ is said to satisfy this identical inclusion if for every assignment of the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ to elements of $S$, the value of $w$ in $S$ coincides with the value of $w_i$ for at least one index $i$. (Thus an ordinary identity $w = w_1$ is the special case in which the right-hand set is a singleton.)

Two semigroups $S$ and $T$ are called inclusively equivalent if they satisfy exactly the same identical inclusions. Equivalently, they generate the same inclusive variety, where the inclusive variety generated by a class of semigroups is the class of all semigroups satisfying every identical inclusion satisfied by every member of the generating class.

Problem. For each of the following basic classes of semigroups, give a complete classification of its members up to inclusive equivalence:

(a) nilsemigroups,
(b) nilpotent semigroups,
(c) periodic Clifford semigroups (semilattices of groups whose maximal subgroups are periodic),
(d) finite groups,
(e) cyclic $p$-groups (for each prime $p$).

That is, in each class describe explicitly the equivalence classes of the inclusive-equivalence relation, equivalently parametrize the inclusive varieties generated by single members of the class.
